triplet: Cartography Sidequest: prove to the machine you have surveyed every inch of your own cage.
Level Goal: reach the end of the level. Your reward is a slightly harder level.
The Maze, a cognitive loop: find an exit to the level. Spoilers, there is no outside.
It's All Upstairs From Here: ascend a tower to fight a guy who could have met you in the lobby.
Run or Die: go that way and don't stop. The illusion of choice, accelerated.
Escape Sequence: run away from danger until you reach safety. Safety is a cutscene.
Rise to the Challenge: climb up until you reach safety. Gravity is now a microtransaction.
Broken Bridge: you cannot pass until the developers finish coding the next zone.
Boss Battle, a challenging monster who exists solely to gatekeep your dopamine.
Kill Enemies to Open: kill all the monsters in an area. You are the janitor of death.
Mass Monster-Slaughter, the grindset: repetitive labor is fun when it's violent!
20 Bear Asses: retrieve random drops for an NPC, the pinnacle of heroic fetch quests.
Gotta Kill Them All, a hitlist: kill everyone on it. A psychopath's grocery run.
Kill Streak: kill as many as you can without getting hit. Perfect for your anxiety!
Player Versus Environment, the computer controlling the game: the house always wins.
Player Versus Player, divide and conquer: keep the plebs fighting each other.
Escort Mission, a weaker ally in a dangerous area: the ultimate test of your patience.
Gotta Rescue Them All, a hoarding pathology disguised as altruism.
Hold the Line: stand in this circle until we say you can leave.
Save the Princess: rescue someone who's been kidnapped. Again. Try better locks next time.
Fetch Quest: retrieve plot coupons for an NPC. You are an intern with a sword.
Chain of Deals, red tape: trade items for items. Bureaucracy as gameplay.
Product Delivery Ordeal: deliver plot coupons to an NPC. Postmates, but with dragons.
Plot Coupons open the door: the narrative equivalent of a punch card.
Gotta Catch Them All, compulsive capture: turning wildlife preservation into a hostage situation.
Herding Mission: herd animals into an area, because AI pathfinding is a joke we play on you.
NPC Round-Up Mission, cat herding: gather NPCs together. Wrangling digital toddlers.
Live Items: stuffing living creatures into your infinite pocket. Don't think about the ethics.
Companion-Specific Sidequest: earn your ally's favor. Friendship is transactional.
Loyalty Mission: complete your ally's goal so they don't betray you at the finale.
Romance Sidequest, simulated love: select dialogue option C to receive affection.
Cosmetic Award, a shiny hat to validate your hundred hours of meaningless grinding.
Stock Video Game Puzzle, because the ancient architect loved pushing ice blocks around.
Mini-Game: play a smaller game with its own rules. Pacing is a myth.
Variable Player Goals: why save the world when you could be taking photos of frogs?
Instant-Win Condition, deus ex machina: press X to end the simulation.
100% Completion, sunk cost fallacy: your digital grave requires all the shiny trinkets.
Gameplay Grading: play the game as well as possible. The machine judges your worth.
Secret Ending: collect all hidden rocks to learn the true, disappointing lore.
Bragging Rights Reward: an achievement that literally nobody else cares about.
Challenge Run, self-sabotage with optional restrictions, because normal misery wasn't enough.
Self-Imposed Challenge, blindfolded: Stockholm Syndrome, expert edition.
No Item Use for You: hoard the mega-elixirs until the credits roll.
No-Gear Level: a sudden, arbitrary strip search by the developers.
Speedrun, sequence break: skip the story, break the physics.
Stealth-Based Mission: an instant fail state for stepping on a twig.
Timed Mission, a ticking clock: artificial stress for artificial stakes.
No-Damage Run: one microscopic pixel of a hitbox ruins five hours of work.
The Cake is a Lie: your real goal is to destroy the facility. The reward was bait.
Princess in Another Castle, moved goalpost: your reward is a fungal hallucination.
Collect 12 Logs: goals players become too dependent on, forgetting how to actually play.
100 Babies: set your own goals. You are the architect of your own hell.
Scoring Points: watch a digital integer increase. They do nothing, but you feel great.
Experience Grind: repeat the same action until the bar is full. Welcome to middle management.
Gold Sink, a mechanic designed purely to delete the wealth you spent hours accumulating.
Hero Must Survive: game over, flip the table. Good thing you're not the hero.
